purpose: Restore a green main and close the availability gap the red run exposed. The Kubernetes acceptance gate deletes one PgBouncer replica and requires zero readiness failures; on 3a8bc974b it got three 503s. The readiness handler already carries a 15-second grace window written for exactly that event - its test is named for the PgBouncer peer failover - but the window lives on the error path and only catches a rejected promise. Deleting a pooler pod does not reject: packets stop arriving and the query hangs, so the handler never leaves its try block, kubelet's 3-second probe timeout expires first, the pod leaves endpoints and ingress answers 503. The control existed, was built for this event, was tested in the shape of failure that does not occur, and was bypassed by the shape that does.
requiredInvariants: The deadline converts a hang into the failure shape the grace window already survives. It does not widen the window: after 15 seconds with no successful read, readiness still fails closed, and that holds for a hang exactly as it held for an error.

The deadline is strictly below the readiness probe's timeoutSeconds. A bound at or above it is not a bound at all - kubelet counts its own timeout first, the pod leaves endpoints, and the deadline means nothing. The test reads that number out of infra/helm/grainflow/values.yaml rather than restating it, so tightening the manifest fails the check too.

The pending query keeps a rejection handler attached when the deadline wins, so a database error arriving late is swallowed rather than surfacing as an unhandled rejection in a process the probe is judging.
The acceptance gate is not weakened. It still allows zero failures across 60 polls; what changes is that the application now holds the property under a hang instead of holding it by luck.

PgBouncer's preStop closes the ordering that produces the disturbance: the process is signalled only after endpoint removal has had time to propagate. terminationGracePeriodSeconds is raised to cover the added window so the drain is not truncated.
No ASVS requirement is claimed by this pass. It is availability and a red main, not a matrix control, and recording it as ASVS progress would be exactly the substitution this programme forbids.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no new dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.

One outstanding database read per process, not one per probe. The deadline releases the handler but does not stop the query, which keeps its pool connection until the database answers. The probe fires every five seconds, so a read started per probe would exhaust the Prisma pool within a minute of a stall and stop not readiness but all API traffic, including traffic that never touches the database. Probes share the in-flight read; there may be any number of waiters and exactly one held connection.
acceptance: Three mutations, each caught: removing the deadline fails all three stall tests by timeout - the handler never returns, which is the production symptom itself; raising the deadline to the probe timeout fails 2; tightening the manifest's probe timeout to 1s fails the boundary test with 'Expected: < 1000, Received: 1500', proving the check reads the manifest instead of restating a constant.
tsc exit 0. telemetry-config and pre-auth-rate-limit suites unaffected: 34 of 34 across the three.

Terminal proof is the acceptance gate itself on exact head: the multi-node kind job must reach the PgBouncer peer-deletion probe and record zero failures. A green unit suite is not that proof and is not offered as it.

Found by review on #4830 and fixed rather than argued with: the first version abandoned the timed-out query's result while the query itself kept running, so each probe started another. The mutation reproduces the reviewer's scenario exactly - three probes during a stall start three further queries (4 calls) without coalescing and one (2 calls) with it. health.controller.spec.ts now 16 of 16, up from 14.

Also raised by that review: adding this scope manifest in the implementation commit is self-authorizing. Not changed here, and answered on the PR. The mechanism (scripts/p7-source-controlled-scope.mjs, resolved by p7-autopilot-guard.sh on GITHUB_HEAD_REF) is pre-existing on main and is what every recent pass in this programme uses; the guard passes; and AGENTS.md L95-L97, which the finding cites, is the reviewer instruction to review the diff rather than the agent report, not a requirement that scopes be registered in a prior commit. The general observation that a same-commit manifest carries its own authority is a governance-design question for the owner, not something to restructure inside a readiness fix.
